title.zh: 卷四百七十一 列傳第二百三十 姦臣一 蔡確 吳處厚 邢恕 呂惠卿 章惇 曾布 安惇
title.en: Volume 471 Biographies 230: Treacherous Officials 1: Cai Que, Wu Chuhou, Xing Shu, Lu Huiqing, Zhang Dun, Ceng Bu, an Dun
title.raw: 卷四百七十一 列傳第二百三十 姦臣一 蔡確 吳處厚 邢恕 呂惠卿 章惇 曾布 安惇 Volume 471 Biographies 230: Treacherous Officials 1: Cai Que, Wu Chuhou, Xing Shu, Lu Huiqing, Zhang Dun, Ceng Bu, an Dun

sentences.zh: 蔡確吳處厚 附 邢恕 呂惠卿 章惇 曾布 安惇

translations.literal: Cai Que and Wu Chuhou, with appendices on Xing Shu, Lü Huiqing, Zhang Dun, Zeng Bu, and An Dun
translations.idiomatic: Cai Que and Wu Chuhou, with appendices on Xing Shu, Lü Huiqing, Zhang Dun, Zeng Bu, and An Dun

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「陽卦多陰，陰卦多陽。」

translations.literal: The Book of Changes says: "Yang trigrams contain many yin lines; yin trigrams contain many yang lines."
translations.idiomatic: The Book of Changes says: "Yang trigrams contain many yin lines; yin trigrams contain many yang lines."

sentences.zh: 君子雖多，小人用事，其象為陰；

translations.literal: Though gentlemen may be many, if petty men hold power, the image is yin;"
translations.idiomatic: Though gentlemen may be many, if petty men hold power, the image is yin;

sentences.zh: 小人雖多，君子用事，其象為陽。

translations.literal: though petty men may be many, if gentlemen hold power, the image is yang.
translations.idiomatic: though petty men may be many, if gentlemen hold power, the image is yang.

sentences.zh: 宋初，五星聚奎，占者以為人才眾多之兆。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Song, the five planets gathered in the Kui asterism, and diviners took this as an omen that talent would be abundant.
translations.idiomatic: At the founding of the Song, the five planets gathered in the Kui asterism, and diviners took it as a sign that men of talent would be plentiful.

sentences.zh: 然終宋之世，賢哲不乏，奸邪亦多。

translations.literal: Yet throughout the Song dynasty, worthy and wise men were not lacking, and treacherous and wicked men were also many.
translations.idiomatic: Yet throughout the Song dynasty, worthy and wise men were never lacking—and treacherous and wicked men were never in short supply either.

sentences.zh: 方其盛時，君子秉政，小人聽命，為患亦鮮。

translations.literal: When the dynasty was at its height, gentlemen held government and petty men obeyed orders, so harm was also rare.
translations.idiomatic: When the dynasty was at its height, gentlemen held power and petty men obeyed orders, so the harm they could do was slight.

sentences.zh: 及其衰也，小人得志，逞其狡謀，壅閼上聽，變易國是，賊虐忠直，屏棄善良，君子在野，無救禍亂。

translations.literal: When it declined, petty men got their way, gave free rein to their cunning schemes, blocked what reached the ruler's ears, altered the fundamental policies of the state, treated the loyal and upright as enemies and abused them, cast out the good, and gentlemen remained in the wilds with no power to avert disaster and disorder.
translations.idiomatic: When it declined, petty men got their way. They gave free rein to their cunning schemes, blocked what reached the ruler's ears, altered the fundamental policies of the state, treated the loyal and upright as enemies and abused them, cast out the good, and left gentlemen stranded outside office with no power to avert disaster and disorder.

sentences.zh: 有國家者，正邪之辨，可不慎乎！

translations.literal: For one who possesses a state, can the distinction between the upright and the wicked be treated without caution!
translations.idiomatic: For one who holds a state in his hands, can the distinction between the upright and the wicked be treated lightly!

sentences.zh: 作《奸臣傳》。

translations.literal: Therefore I compose the "Biographies of Treacherous Ministers."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I compose the "Biographies of Treacherous Ministers."

sentences.zh: 蔡確字持正，泉州晉江人，父徙陳。

translations.literal: Cai Que, courtesy name Chizheng, was a native of Jinjiang in Quanzhou; his father moved to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Cai Que, courtesy name Chizheng, was a native of Jinjiang in Quanzhou; his father later moved the family to Chen.

sentences.zh: 確有智數，尚氣，不謹細行。

translations.literal: Que was clever and resourceful, valued bold spirit, and was not careful in small conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Que was clever and resourceful, proud and spirited, and careless about propriety in small matters.

sentences.zh: 第進士，調邠州司理參軍，以賄聞。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination, was assigned as judicial assistant in Bin Prefecture, and became known for taking bribes.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was assigned as judicial assistant in Bin Prefecture, where he became known for taking bribes.

sentences.zh: 轉運使薛向行部，欲按治，見其儀觀秀偉，召與語，奇之，更加延譽。

translations.literal: When the transport commissioner Xue Xiang toured the circuit and intended to investigate and punish him, he saw Que's bearing was handsome and imposing, summoned him to talk, was impressed, and praised him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: When the transport commissioner Xue Xiang toured the circuit and intended to investigate and punish him, he saw that Que's bearing was handsome and imposing, summoned him to talk, was impressed, and praised him all the more.

sentences.zh: 韓絳宣撫陝西，見所制樂語，以為材，薦于弟開封尹維，辟管幹右廂公事，維去而確至。

translations.literal: When Han Jiang pacified Shaanxi, he saw the ceremonial lyrics Que had composed, considered him talented, recommended him to his younger brother Wei, the prefect of Kaifeng, who appointed him to manage affairs in the Right Wing office; Wei departed and Que arrived.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Jiang was pacifying Shaanxi, he saw the ceremonial lyrics Que had composed, considered him talented, and recommended him to his younger brother Wei, the prefect of Kaifeng. Wei appointed Que to manage affairs in the Right Wing office; Wei later departed, and Que took up the post.

sentences.zh: 舊制當庭參，確不肯，後尹劉庠責之，確曰：「唐藩鎮自置掾屬，故有是禮。

translations.literal: By old regulation he was to attend court audience, but Que refused. Later the prefect Liu Xiang rebuked him. Que said: "In Tang times the frontier military governors appointed their own staff, and therefore there was such a ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: By old regulation he was to attend court audience, but Que refused. Later the prefect Liu Xiang rebuked him. Que said: "In Tang times the frontier military governors appointed their own staff, and therefore there was such a ceremony.

sentences.zh: 今輦轂下比肩事主，雖故事不可用。」

translations.literal: Now under the imperial capital we stand shoulder to shoulder in serving our lord; though it is an old precedent, it cannot be used."
translations.idiomatic: Now under the imperial capital we stand shoulder to shoulder in serving our lord; though it is an old precedent, it cannot be used."

sentences.zh: 遂乞解職。

translations.literal: He then requested to be relieved of his post.
translations.idiomatic: He then requested to be relieved of his post.

sentences.zh: 王安石薦確，徙為三班主簿。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi recommended Que, and he was transferred to be chief clerk of the Third Class.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi recommended Que, and he was transferred to be chief clerk of the Third Class.

sentences.zh: 用鄧綰薦，為監察御史裏行。

translations.literal: On Deng Wan's recommendation, he became acting investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: On Deng Wan's recommendation, he became acting investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 王韶開熙河，多貸公錢，秦帥郭逵劾其罪，詔使杜純鞫治得實。

translations.literal: Wang Shao opened the Xihe region and borrowed much public money; the Qin circuit commander Guo Kui impeached him for the offense, and an edict sent Du Chun to investigate and establish the facts.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shao opened the Xihe region and borrowed large sums of public money. The Qin circuit commander Guo Kui impeached him for the offense, and an edict sent Du Chun to investigate; the charges were found to be true.

sentences.zh: 安石卻其牘，更遣確，確希意直韶，逵、純獲譴。

translations.literal: Anshi rejected the memorial and instead sent Que; Que pleased his intent and cleared Shao, and Kui and Chun were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi rejected the memorial and instead sent Que; Que read his intent and cleared Shao, and Kui and Chun were punished.

sentences.zh: 確善觀人主意，與時上下，知神宗已厭安石，因安石乘馬入宣德門與衛士競，即疏其過以賈直。

translations.literal: Que was skilled at reading the ruler's intent and adjusted with the times; knowing that Emperor Shenzong had already grown weary of Anshi, when Anshi rode his horse through the Xuande Gate and quarreled with the guards, Que immediately memorialized his fault to buy favor.
translations.idiomatic: Que was skilled at reading the ruler's intent and adjusted with the times. Knowing that Emperor Shenzong had already grown weary of Anshi, when Anshi rode his horse through the Xuande Gate and quarreled with the guards, Que immediately memorialized his fault to buy favor.

sentences.zh: 加直集賢院，遷御史知雜事。

translations.literal: He was added as a scholar of the Jixian Academy and promoted to supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was added as a scholar of the Jixian Academy and promoted to supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 範子淵浚河之役，知制誥熊本按行以為非是，為子淵所訟，確劾本附文彥博，黜之，代為知制誥、知諫院兼判司農寺。

translations.literal: In Fan Ziyuan's river-dredging project, the drafter of edicts Xiong Ben inspected the work and judged it unsound; Ziyuan sued him, and Que impeached Ben for siding with Wen Yanbo, had him dismissed, and took his place as drafter of edicts, director of the Remonstrance Bureau, and concurrent administrator of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In Fan Ziyuan's river-dredging project, the drafter of edicts Xiong Ben inspected the work and judged it unsound. Ziyuan sued him, and Que impeached Ben for siding with Wen Yanbo, had him dismissed, and took his place as drafter of edicts, director of the Remonstrance Bureau, and concurrent administrator of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 三司使沈括謁宰相吳充論免役法，確言括為近臣，見朝廷法令未便，不公言之而私語執政，意王安石既去，新法可搖耳。

translations.literal: The Three Departments commissioner Shen Kuo visited the chief councilor Wu Chong to discuss the exemption-from-corvée law. Que said that Kuo, as a close minister, saw that a court law was unsuitable yet did not speak openly but whispered to those in power, meaning that now that Wang Anshi was gone, the new laws could be shaken.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments commissioner Shen Kuo visited the chief councilor Wu Chong to discuss the exemption-from-corvée law. Que said that Kuo, as a close minister, saw that a court law was unsuitable yet did not speak openly but whispered to those in power—meaning that now that Wang Anshi was gone, the new laws could be shaken.

sentences.zh: 括坐黜知宣州。

translations.literal: Kuo was demoted for this and made prefect of Xuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Kuo was demoted for this and made prefect of Xuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 開封鞫相州民訟，事連判官陳安民，安民令其甥文及甫求援於充之子安持，及甫，充婿也。

translations.literal: Kaifeng tried a lawsuit among the people of Xiang Prefecture, and the matter implicated the assistant prefect Chen Anmin; Anmin had his nephew Wen Jifu seek help from Chong's son Anchí, and Jifu was Chong's son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: Kaifeng tried a lawsuit among the people of Xiang Prefecture, and the matter implicated the assistant prefect Chen Anmin. Anmin had his nephew Wen Jifu seek help from Chong's son Anchí; Jifu was Chong's son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 確言事關大臣，非開封可了，遂移御史台。

translations.literal: Que said the matter involved a great minister and could not be settled by Kaifeng, so the case was transferred to the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: Que said the matter involved a great minister and could not be settled by Kaifeng, so the case was transferred to the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 時獄起皇城，卒事多不仇。

translations.literal: At the time a case arose in the Imperial City, and in the end the facts did not match.
translations.idiomatic: At the time a case arose in the Imperial City, and in the end the facts did not match.

sentences.zh: 中丞鄧潤甫，御史上官均按之，與府獄同。

translations.literal: The vice censor Deng Runfu and the investigating censor Shangguan Jun investigated it and reached the same conclusion as the prefectural court.
translations.idiomatic: The vice censor Deng Runfu and the investigating censor Shangguan Jun investigated it and reached the same conclusion as the prefectural court.

sentences.zh: 王珪奏遣確詣台參治，確鍛煉為獄，潤甫、均不能制，密奏確慘掠諸囚。

translations.literal: Wang Gui memorialized that Que be sent to the Censorate to take part in the trial; Que forged the case into a criminal prosecution, Runfu and Jun could not restrain him, and secretly memorialized that Que cruelly tortured the prisoners.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui memorialized that Que be sent to the Censorate to take part in the trial. Que forged the case into a criminal prosecution; Runfu and Jun could not restrain him and secretly memorialized that Que cruelly tortured the prisoners.

sentences.zh: 確伺知之，即劾二人庇有罪，且詐使吏為使者慮問，囚稱冤，輒苦辱之。

translations.literal: Que learned of this by spying, immediately impeached the two for shielding the guilty, and also had clerks falsely pose as envoys to conduct inquiries; whenever prisoners claimed injustice, he harshly humiliated them.
translations.idiomatic: Que learned of this by spying, immediately impeached the two for shielding the guilty, and also had clerks falsely pose as envoys to conduct inquiries; whenever prisoners claimed injustice, he harshly humiliated them.

sentences.zh: 帝頗疑其濫，連遣諫官及內侍審直，皆怖畏，言不冤，由是潤甫、均皆罷，而確得中丞，猶領司農，凡常平、免役法皆成其手。

translations.literal: The emperor was somewhat suspicious of the excess, and repeatedly sent remonstrance officials and inner attendants to review the case; all were terrified and said there was no injustice. Thereupon Runfu and Jun were both dismissed, Que became vice censor while still heading the Ministry of Revenue, and the Ever-Normal Granary and exemption-from-corvée laws were all shaped by his hand.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was somewhat suspicious of the excess and repeatedly sent remonstrance officials and inner attendants to review the case; all were terrified and said there was no injustice. Thereupon Runfu and Jun were both dismissed, Que became vice censor while still heading the Ministry of Revenue, and the Ever-Normal Granary and exemption-from-corvée laws were all shaped by his hand.

sentences.zh: 太學生虞蕃訟學官，確深探其獄，連引朝士，自翰林學士許將以下皆逮捕械系，令獄卒與同寢處，飲食旋溷共為一室，設大盆於前，凡羹飯餅胾舉投其中，以杓混攪，分飼之如犬豕。

translations.literal: The Imperial University student Yu Fan sued the school officials; Que dug deeply into the case, implicated court gentlemen one after another, and from Hanlin academician Xu Jiang downward all were arrested and shackled. He had jailers sleep in the same quarters with them, eat and drink and use the privy in one room, set a large basin before them, threw all soup, rice, cakes, and meat into it, stirred them with a ladle, and fed them as one would dogs and pigs.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial University student Yu Fan sued the school officials. Que dug deeply into the case and implicated court gentlemen one after another; from Hanlin academician Xu Jiang downward, all were arrested and shackled. He had jailers sleep in the same quarters with them, eat and drink and use the privy in one room, set a large basin before them, threw all soup, rice, cakes, and meat into it, stirred them with a ladle, and fed them as one would dogs and pigs.

sentences.zh: 久系不問，幸而得問，無一事不承。

translations.literal: Long detained without questioning, when at last they were questioned, there was not one matter they did not confess.
translations.idiomatic: Long detained without questioning, when at last they were questioned, there was not one matter they did not confess.

sentences.zh: 遂劾參知政事元絳有所屬請，絳出知亳州；

translations.literal: He then impeached the vice grand councilor Yuan Jiang for having made requests on someone's behalf, and Jiang was sent out as prefect of Bo Prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: He then impeached the vice grand councilor Yuan Jiang for having made requests on someone's behalf, and Jiang was sent out as prefect of Bo Prefecture;

sentences.zh: 確代其位。

translations.literal: Que took his place.
translations.idiomatic: Que took his place.

sentences.zh: 確自知制誥為御史中丞、參知政事，皆以起獄奪人位而居之，士大夫交口咄罵，而確自以為得計也。

translations.literal: From drafter of edicts to supervising censor to vice grand councilor, Que had each time risen by launching cases, seized others' positions, and occupied them; scholar-officials cursed him with one voice, yet Que thought he had got his way.
translations.idiomatic: From drafter of edicts to supervising censor to vice grand councilor, Que had each time risen by launching cases, seizing others' positions, and occupying them. Scholar-officials cursed him with one voice, yet Que thought he had got his way.

sentences.zh: 吳充數為帝言新法不便，欲稍去其甚者，確曰：「曹參與蕭何有隙，至代為相，一遵何約束。

translations.literal: Wu Chong repeatedly told the emperor that the new laws were inconvenient and wished to remove somewhat the most severe parts. Que said: "Cao Shen and Xiao He had a rift, yet when Cao replaced him as chancellor he followed Xiao He's rules entirely.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chong repeatedly told the emperor that the new laws were inconvenient and wished to remove somewhat the most severe parts. Que said: "Cao Shen and Xiao He had a rift, yet when Cao replaced him as chancellor he followed Xiao He's rules entirely.

sentences.zh: 今陛下所自建立，豈容一人挾怨而壞之。」

translations.literal: What Your Majesty has established by your own hand—how can one man, nursing a grudge, be allowed to ruin it?"
translations.idiomatic: What Your Majesty has established by your own hand—how can one man, nursing a grudge, be allowed to ruin it?"

sentences.zh: 法遂不變。

translations.literal: The laws therefore were not changed.
translations.idiomatic: The laws therefore were not changed.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年，拜尚書右僕射兼中書侍郎。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng, he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng, he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時富弼在西京，上言蔡確小人，不宜大用。

translations.literal: At the time Fu Bi was in the Western Capital and memorialized that Cai Que was a petty man and should not be greatly employed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Fu Bi was in the Western Capital and memorialized that Cai Que was a petty man and should not be greatly employed.

sentences.zh: 確既相，屬興羅織之獄，縉紳士大夫重足而立矣。

translations.literal: Once Que became chief councilor, he repeatedly launched fabricated prosecutions, and gentry and scholar-officials stood as though with both feet together in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Once Que became chief councilor, he repeatedly launched fabricated prosecutions, and gentry and scholar-officials stood as though with both feet together in fear.

sentences.zh: 初議官制，蓋仿《唐六典》，事無大小，並中書取旨，門下審覆，尚書受而行之，三省分班奏事，柄歸中書。

translations.literal: When the bureaucracy was first redesigned, it largely followed the Tang Six Statutes: matters great and small were all taken for instruction by the Secretariat, reviewed by the Chancellery, and received and executed by the Department of State Affairs; the three departments reported in separate shifts, and power returned to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When the bureaucracy was first redesigned, it largely followed the Tang Six Statutes: matters great and small were all taken for instruction by the Secretariat, reviewed by the Chancellery, and received and executed by the Department of State Affairs; the three departments reported in separate shifts, and power returned to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 確說王珪曰：「公久在相位，必得中書令。」

translations.literal: Que persuaded Wang Gui, saying: "You have long been in the chief councilor's seat; you are sure to receive the post of Director of the Secretariat."
translations.idiomatic: Que persuaded Wang Gui, saying: "You have long been in the chief councilor's seat; you are sure to receive the post of Director of the Secretariat."

sentences.zh: 珪信不疑。

translations.literal: Gui believed it without doubt.
translations.idiomatic: Gui believed it without doubt.

sentences.zh: 確乃言於帝曰：「三省長官位高，不須置令，但令左右僕射分兼兩省侍郎足矣。」

translations.literal: Que then said to the emperor: "The heads of the three departments are too high in rank; there is no need to appoint directors. It is enough to have the left and right vice directors concurrently hold the vice directorships of the two secretariats."
translations.idiomatic: Que then said to the emperor: "The heads of the three departments are too high in rank; there is no need to appoint directors. It is enough to have the left and right vice directors concurrently hold the vice directorships of the two secretariats."

sentences.zh: 帝以為然。

translations.literal: The emperor thought this correct.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thought this correct.

sentences.zh: 故確名為次相，實顓大政，珪以左僕射兼門下，拱手而已。

translations.literal: Therefore Que was nominally the second chief councilor but in fact monopolized major policy; Gui, as Left Vice Director concurrently holding the Chancellery, could only fold his hands.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Que was nominally the second chief councilor but in fact monopolized major policy; Gui, as Left Vice Director concurrently holding the Chancellery, could only fold his hands.

sentences.zh: 帝雖以次敘相珪、確，然不加禮重，屢因微失罰金，每罰輒門謝。

translations.literal: Although the emperor ranked Gui and Que in order as chief councilors, he did not treat them with special honor; repeatedly for minor faults he fined them, and each time they were fined they had to apologize at the gate.
translations.idiomatic: Although the emperor ranked Gui and Que in order as chief councilors, he did not treat them with special honor; repeatedly for minor faults he fined them, and each time they were fined they had to apologize at the gate.

sentences.zh: 宰相罰金門謝，前此未有，人皆恥之。

translations.literal: Chief councilors fined and apologizing at the gate—there had never been such a thing before, and all were ashamed of it.
translations.idiomatic: Chief councilors fined and apologizing at the gate—there had never been such a thing before, and all were ashamed of it.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，轉左僕射。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, Que was transferred to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, Que was transferred to Left Vice Director.

sentences.zh: 韓縝入相中書，用其兩侄為列卿，確風御史中丞黃履劾縝。

translations.literal: Han Zong entered the Secretariat as chief councilor and appointed his two nephews to ministerial posts; Que prompted the supervising censor Huang Lü to impeach Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Han Zong entered the Secretariat as chief councilor and appointed his two nephews to ministerial posts; Que prompted the supervising censor Huang Lü to impeach Zong.

sentences.zh: 始詔三省，凡取旨事及台諫官章疏，並執政同進擬，不專屬中書。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued to the three departments that all matters taken for instruction and memorials from censorial and remonstrance officials were to be jointly submitted for appointment by all chief councilors, and were not to belong exclusively to the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued to the three departments that all matters taken for instruction and memorials from censorial and remonstrance officials were to be jointly submitted for appointment by all chief councilors, and were not to belong exclusively to the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 蓋確畏失權，又復改制也。

translations.literal: This was because Que feared losing power and again reshaped the system.
translations.idiomatic: This was because Que feared losing power and again reshaped the system.

sentences.zh: 初，神宗疾革，王珪議建儲事，確與同列皆在側，知狀。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Emperor Shenzong was gravely ill, Wang Gui discussed establishing the heir; Que and his colleagues were all at the side and knew the circumstances.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Emperor Shenzong was gravely ill, Wang Gui discussed establishing the heir; Que and his colleagues were all at the side and knew the circumstances.

sentences.zh: 確自見得罪于世，陰與章惇、邢恕等合志邪謀，謂珪實懷異意，賴己擁護，故不得逞。

translations.literal: Que saw that he had offended the world and secretly joined in wicked schemes with Zhang Dun, Xing Shu, and others, saying that Gui in fact harbored ulterior intent and that only because Que had supported the heir could Gui's designs not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Que saw that he had offended the world and secretly joined in wicked schemes with Zhang Dun, Xing Shu, and others, saying that Gui in fact harbored ulterior intent and that only because Que had supported the heir could Gui's designs not succeed.

sentences.zh: 確奉使陵下，韓縝白髮其端，事浸籍籍。

translations.literal: When Que was on a mission at the imperial tombs, Han Zong reported the matter at its beginning, and the affair gradually became widely known.
translations.idiomatic: When Que was on a mission at the imperial tombs, Han Zong reported the matter at its beginning, and the affair gradually became widely known.

sentences.zh: 既失勢，愈怨望，恕又益為往來造言，識者以為憂，未有以發也。

translations.literal: Having lost power, he grew ever more resentful; Shu further spread rumors back and forth, and those who understood the situation were worried, but there was as yet no way to expose it.
translations.idiomatic: Having lost power, he grew ever more resentful. Shu further spread rumors back and forth, and those who understood the situation were worried, but there was as yet no way to expose it.

sentences.zh: 確在安陸，嘗游車蓋亭，賦詩十章，知漢陽軍吳處厚上之，以為皆涉譏訕，其用郝處俊上元間諫高宗欲傳位天後事，以斥東朝，語尤切害。

translations.literal: When Que was in Anlu, he once visited the Chariot Canopy Pavilion and composed ten poems; Wu Chuhou, military prefect of Hanyang, submitted them, saying they all involved mockery and satire. One used the matter of Hao Chujun remonstrating with Emperor Gaozong during the Shangyuan reign when Gaozong wished to abdicate to Empress Wu, to criticize the Eastern Court; the language was especially cutting and harmful.
translations.idiomatic: When Que was in Anlu, he once visited the Chariot Canopy Pavilion and composed ten poems. Wu Chuhou, military prefect of Hanyang, submitted them, saying they all involved mockery and satire. One used the matter of Hao Chujun remonstrating with Emperor Gaozong during the Shangyuan reign when Gaozong wished to abdicate to Empress Wu, to criticize the Eastern Court; the language was especially cutting and harmful.

sentences.zh: 於是左諫議大夫梁燾、右諫議大夫范祖禹、左司諫吳安詩、右司諫王岩叟、右正言劉安世，進上章乞正確罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Left Remonstrance Grandee Liang Tao, Right Remonstrance Grandee Fan Zuyu, Left Secretariat Remonstrance Official Wu Anshi, Right Secretariat Remonstrance Official Wang Yansou, and Right Rectifier Liu Anshi submitted memorials requesting that Que's crimes be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the Left Remonstrance Grandee Liang Tao, Right Remonstrance Grandee Fan Zuyu, Left Secretariat Remonstrance Official Wu Anshi, Right Secretariat Remonstrance Official Wang Yansou, and Right Rectifier Liu Anshi submitted memorials requesting that Que's crimes be punished.

sentences.zh: 詔確具析，確自辯甚悉。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Que to provide a detailed explanation; Que defended himself at great length.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered Que to provide a detailed explanation; Que defended himself at great length.

sentences.zh: 安世等又言確罪狀著明，何待具析，此乃大臣委曲為之地耳。

translations.literal: Anshi and the others again said Que's crimes were clear—why wait for a detailed explanation? This was merely great ministers making excuses for him.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi and the others again said Que's crimes were clear—why wait for a detailed explanation? This was merely great ministers making excuses for him.

sentences.zh: 遂貶光祿卿、分司南京，再責英州別駕、新州安置。

translations.literal: He was then demoted to Grandee of Splendid Happiness with nominal duty in the Southern Capital, and again punished as assistant prefect of Ying Prefecture and assigned to Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was then demoted to Grandee of Splendid Happiness with nominal duty in the Southern Capital, and again punished as assistant prefect of Ying Prefecture and assigned to Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宰相范純仁、左丞王存坐廉前出語救確，御史李常、盛陶、翟恩、趙挺之、王彭年坐不舉劾，中書舍人彭汝大力礰坐封還詞命，皆罷去。

translations.literal: Chief councilor Fan Chunren and Left Vice Director Wang Cun were punished for having spoken earlier to save Que; investigating censors Li Chang, Sheng Tao, Zhai En, Zhao Tingzhi, and Wang Pengnian were punished for failing to impeach; Secretariat drafter Peng Ruli was punished for returning the appointment edict sealed; all were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Chief councilor Fan Chunren and Left Vice Director Wang Cun were punished for having spoken earlier to save Que; investigating censors Li Chang, Sheng Tao, Zhai En, Zhao Tingzhi, and Wang Pengnian were punished for failing to impeach; Secretariat drafter Peng Ruli was punished for returning the appointment edict sealed; all were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 確後卒於貶所。

translations.literal: Que later died in exile.
translations.idiomatic: Que later died in exile.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，下詔暴群奸之罪，貶確武泰軍節度副使，竄懋英州，凡所與濫恩，一切削奪，天下快之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, he issued an edict exposing the crimes of the group of traitors, demoted Que to military commissioner deputy of Wutai Army, and banished him to Ying Prefecture; all improper favors he had received were entirely stripped away, and the realm rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong ascended the throne, he issued an edict exposing the crimes of the group of traitors, demoted Que to military commissioner deputy of Wutai Army, and banished him to Ying Prefecture. All improper favors he had received were entirely stripped away, and the realm rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 吳處厚 附

translations.literal: Wu Chuhou — appendix
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chuhou — appendix

sentences.zh: 吳處厚者，邵武人，登進士第。

translations.literal: Wu Chuhou was a native of Shaowu and passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chuhou was a native of Shaowu and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 仁宗屢喪皇嗣，處厚上言：「臣嘗讀《史記》，考趙氏廢興本末，當屠岸賈之難，程嬰、公孫杵臼盡死以全趙孤。

translations.literal: Emperor Renzong repeatedly lost imperial heirs. Chuhou memorialized: "Your subject once read the Records of the Grand Historian and examined the rise and fall of the Zhao house. During the disaster of Tu'an Gu, Cheng Ying and Gongsun Chujiu gave their lives to preserve the Zhao orphan.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Renzong repeatedly lost imperial heirs. Chuhou memorialized: "Your subject once read the Records of the Grand Historian and examined the rise and fall of the Zhao house. During the disaster of Tu'an Gu, Cheng Ying and Gongsun Chujiu gave their lives to preserve the Zhao orphan.

sentences.zh: 宋有天下，二人忠義未見褒表，宜訪其墓域，建為其祠。」

translations.literal: Since the Song possess the realm, these two men's loyalty and righteousness have not been honored; their tombs should be sought out and shrines built for them."
translations.idiomatic: Since the Song possess the realm, these two men's loyalty and righteousness have not been honored; their tombs should be sought out and shrines built for them."

sentences.zh: 帝覽其疏矍然，即以處厚為將作丞，訪得兩墓于絳，封侯立廟。

translations.literal: The emperor, reading his memorial, was startled and immediately appointed Chuhou as director of palace construction; the two tombs were found in Jiang, and marquisates were conferred and temples established.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, reading his memorial, was startled and immediately appointed Chuhou as director of palace construction. The two tombs were found in Jiang, and marquisates were conferred and temples established.

sentences.zh: 始，蔡確嘗從處厚學賦，及作相，處厚通箋乞憐，確無汲引意。

translations.literal: At first Cai Que had studied fu composition under Chuhou; when he became chief councilor, Chuhou sent a letter asking for favor, but Que had no intention of promoting him.
translations.idiomatic: At first Cai Que had studied fu composition under Chuhou; when he became chief councilor, Chuhou sent a letter asking for favor, but Que had no intention of promoting him.

sentences.zh: 王珪用為大理丞。

translations.literal: Wang Gui employed him as assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Gui employed him as assistant director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 王安禮、舒亶相攻，事下大理，處厚知安禮與珪善，論亶用官燭為自盜。

translations.literal: Wang Anli and Shu Dan attacked each other; the matter went down to the Court of Judicial Review. Chuhou knew Anli was on good terms with Gui and judged Dan guilty of embezzling official candles for personal use.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anli and Shu Dan attacked each other; the matter went down to the Court of Judicial Review. Chuhou knew Anli was on good terms with Gui and judged Dan guilty of embezzling official candles for personal use.

sentences.zh: 確密遣達意救亶，處厚不從，確怒欲逐之，未果。

translations.literal: Que secretly sent word to save Dan; Chuhou would not comply. Que grew angry and wished to drive him out, but did not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Que secretly sent word to save Dan; Chuhou would not comply. Que grew angry and wished to drive him out, but did not succeed.

sentences.zh: 珪請除處厚館職，確又沮之。

translations.literal: Gui requested that Chuhou be given an academy post; Que again obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: Gui requested that Chuhou be given an academy post; Que again obstructed it.

sentences.zh: 珪為永裕山陵使，辟掌箋奏。

translations.literal: Gui served as commissioner for the Yongyu imperial tombs and appointed Chuhou to manage memorial drafts.
translations.idiomatic: Gui served as commissioner for the Yongyu imperial tombs and appointed Chuhou to manage memorial drafts.

sentences.zh: 確代使，出知通利軍，又徙知漢陽，處厚不悅。

translations.literal: Que replaced him as commissioner; Chuhou was sent out as military prefect of Tongli Army and later transferred to Hanyang, and Chuhou was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Que replaced him as commissioner. Chuhou was sent out as military prefect of Tongli Army and later transferred to Hanyang, and he was displeased.

sentences.zh: 元祐中，確知安州，郡有靜江卒當戍漢陽，確固不遣，處厚怒曰：「爾在廟堂時數陷我，今比郡作守，猶爾邪？」

translations.literal: During the Yuanyou era, Que was prefect of An Prefecture; the prefecture had Jingjiang troops who were to garrison Hanyang, but Que firmly refused to send them. Chuhou angrily said: "When you were in the hall of state you repeatedly trapped me; now that you are prefect of a neighboring command, you still act this way?"
translations.idiomatic: During the Yuanyou era, Que was prefect of An Prefecture. The prefecture had Jingjiang troops who were to garrison Hanyang, but Que firmly refused to send them. Chuhou angrily said: "When you were in the hall of state you repeatedly trapped me; now that you are prefect of a neighboring command, you still act this way?"

sentences.zh: 會得確《車蓋亭詩》，引郝甑山事，乃箋釋上之，云：「郝處俊封甑山公，會高宗欲遜位武后，處俊諫止，今乃以比太皇太后。

translations.literal: It happened that he obtained Que's Chariot Canopy Pavilion poems, which cited the matter of Hao Zengshan; he annotated and submitted them, saying: "Hao Chujun was enfeoffed as Duke of Zengshan; when Emperor Gaozong wished to abdicate to Empress Wu, Hao remonstrated and stopped it—yet now this is used to compare with the Grand Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: It happened that he obtained Que's Chariot Canopy Pavilion poems, which cited the matter of Hao Zengshan; he annotated and submitted them, saying: "Hao Chujun was enfeoffed as Duke of Zengshan; when Emperor Gaozong wished to abdicate to Empress Wu, Hao remonstrated and stopped it—yet now this is used to compare with the Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 且用滄海揚塵事，此蓋時運之大變，尤非佳語。

translations.literal: Moreover it uses the matter of dust rising from the blue sea—this suggests a great change in the times' fortune and is especially not good language.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover it uses the matter of dust rising from the blue sea—this suggests a great change in the times' fortune and is especially not good language.

sentences.zh: 譏謗切害，非所宜言。」

translations.literal: The mockery is cutting and harmful; such things should not be said."
translations.idiomatic: The mockery is cutting and harmful; such things should not be said."

sentences.zh: 確遂南竄。

translations.literal: Que was then banished to the south.
translations.idiomatic: Que was then banished to the south.

sentences.zh: 擢處厚知衛州，然士大夫由此畏惡之，未幾卒。

translations.literal: Chuhou was promoted to prefect of Wei Prefecture, but scholar-officials from this feared and hated him, and before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: Chuhou was promoted to prefect of Wei Prefecture, but scholar-officials from this feared and hated him, and before long he died.

sentences.zh: 紹聖間，追貶歙州別駕。

translations.literal: During the Shaosheng era, he was posthumously demoted to assistant prefect of She Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Shaosheng era, he was posthumously demoted to assistant prefect of She Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 邢恕字和叔，鄭州陽武人。

translations.literal: Xing Shu, courtesy name Heshu, was a native of Yangwu in Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Shu, courtesy name Heshu, was a native of Yangwu in Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 博貫經籍，能文章，喜功名，論古今成敗事，有戰國縱橫氣習。

translations.literal: He was broadly versed in the classics, skilled at writing, fond of fame and achievement, and when discussing success and failure in affairs ancient and modern had the air of Warring States strategists.
translations.idiomatic: He was broadly versed in the classics, skilled at writing, fond of fame and achievement, and when discussing success and failure in affairs ancient and modern had the air of Warring States strategists.

sentences.zh: 從程顥學，因出入司馬光、呂公著門。

translations.literal: He studied under Cheng Hao and thereby came and went in the households of Sima Guang and Lü Gongzhu.
translations.idiomatic: He studied under Cheng Hao and thereby came and went in the households of Sima Guang and Lü Gongzhu.

sentences.zh: 登進士第，補永安主簿。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Yong'an.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed chief clerk of Yong'an.

sentences.zh: 公著薦於朝，得崇文院校書。

translations.literal: Gongzhu recommended him to the court, and he became collator of the Chongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Gongzhu recommended him to the court, and he became collator of the Chongwen Academy.

sentences.zh: 王安石亦愛之，因賓客諭意，使養晦以待用，恕不能從，而對其子雱語新法不便。

translations.literal: Wang Anshi also favored him and through a guest conveyed his intent, telling him to bide his time and await employment; Shu could not comply, and to Anshi's son Bian he spoke of the new laws' inconveniences.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi also favored him and through a guest conveyed his intent, telling him to bide his time and await employment. Shu could not comply, and to Anshi's son Bian he spoke of the new laws' inconveniences.

sentences.zh: 安石怒，諫官亦言新進士未曆官而即處館閣，開奔競路，出知延陵縣。

translations.literal: Anshi grew angry; remonstrance officials also said that a newly passed jinshi who had not yet served in office was immediately placed in the academy, opening a path of frantic competition, and Shu was sent out as magistrate of Yanling County.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi grew angry. Remonstrance officials also said that a newly passed jinshi who had not yet served in office was immediately placed in the academy, opening a path of frantic competition, and Shu was sent out as magistrate of Yanling County.

sentences.zh: 縣廢不復調，浮湛陝、洛間者七年，復為校書。

translations.literal: The county was abolished and he was not reassigned; he drifted between Shaan and Lu for seven years, then again became collator.
translations.idiomatic: The county was abolished and he was not reassigned. He drifted between Shaan and Lu for seven years, then again became collator.

sentences.zh: 吳充用為館閣校勘，歷史館檢討、著作佐郎。

translations.literal: Wu Chong employed him as academy collator; he served as historiographer compiler and assistant director of the Office of Compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Chong employed him as academy collator. He served as historiographer compiler and assistant director of the Office of Compilation.

sentences.zh: 蔡確代充相，盡逐充所用人，恕深居懼及。

translations.literal: When Cai Que replaced Chong as chief councilor, he drove out all whom Chong had employed; Shu lived in seclusion, fearing he would be implicated.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Que replaced Chong as chief councilor, he drove out all whom Chong had employed. Shu lived in seclusion, fearing he would be implicated.

sentences.zh: 神宗見其《送文彥博詩》，稱於確，乃進職方員外郎。

translations.literal: Emperor Shenzong saw his poem "Seeing Off Wen Yanbo" and praised it to Que; he was then promoted to outer-section director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Shenzong saw his poem "Seeing Off Wen Yanbo" and praised it to Que; he was then promoted to outer-section director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 帝有復用光、公著意，確以恕于兩人為門下客，亟結納之。

translations.literal: The emperor had the intent to reuse Guang and Gongzhu; Que, because Shu had been a client in both men's households, quickly cultivated him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had the intent to reuse Guang and Gongzhu. Que, because Shu had been a client in both men's households, quickly cultivated him.

sentences.zh: 恕亦深自附托，乃為確畫策，稍收召名士，于政事微有更革，自是相與如素交。

translations.literal: Shu also deeply attached himself to Que, then plotted strategy for him, gradually recalled famous scholars, and made slight changes in government affairs; from this they were together like old friends.
translations.idiomatic: Shu also threw in his lot with Que, plotted strategy for him, gradually recalled famous scholars, and made slight changes in government affairs. From then on they were together like old friends.

sentences.zh: 帝不豫，恕與確成謀，密語宣仁後之侄公繪、公紀曰：「家有白桃著華，道書言可療上疾。」

translations.literal: When the emperor was unwell, Shu and Que formed a plot and secretly said to Empress Dowager Xuanren's nephews Gong Hui and Gong Ji: "My house has white peaches in bloom; Taoist books say they can cure the emperor's illness."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor was unwell, Shu and Que formed a plot and secretly said to Empress Dowager Xuanren's nephews Gong Hui and Gong Ji: "My house has white peaches in bloom; Taoist books say they can cure the emperor's illness."

sentences.zh: 邀與歸視之。

translations.literal: They invited them to return and look.
translations.idiomatic: They invited them to come back and see.

sentences.zh: 至則執其手曰：「蔡丞相令布腹心，上疾不可諱，延安沖幼，宜早有定論，雍、曹皆賢王也。」

translations.literal: When they arrived, he seized their hands and said: "Chief Councilor Cai sent me to lay bare my heart. The emperor's illness cannot be concealed; Yan'an is young and tender—a decision should be made early. Yong and Cao are both worthy princes."
translations.idiomatic: When they arrived, he seized their hands and said: "Chief Councilor Cai sent me to lay bare my heart. The emperor's illness cannot be concealed; Yan'an is young and tender—a decision should be made early. Yong and Cao are both worthy princes."

sentences.zh: 公繪驚曰：「此何言？

translations.literal: Gong Hui said in alarm: "What words are these?
translations.idiomatic: Gong Hui said in alarm: "What words are these?

sentences.zh: 君欲禍吾家邪！」

translations.literal: Do you wish to bring disaster on my family!"
translations.idiomatic: Do you wish to bring disaster on my family!"

sentences.zh: 急趨出。

translations.literal: He hurried out.
translations.idiomatic: He hurried out.

sentences.zh: 恕計不行，則反宣言太后屬意雍王，與王珪表裏。

translations.literal: When Shu's plan did not succeed, he instead declared that the empress dowager favored Prince Yong and was in league with Wang Gui.
translations.idiomatic: When Shu's plan failed, he instead declared that the empress dowager favored Prince Yong and was in league with Wang Gui.

sentences.zh: 導確約珪入問疾，陽鉤致珪語，使知開封府蔡京伏劍士於外，須珪小持異則執而誅之。

translations.literal: He guided Que to arrange for Gui to enter and inquire after the emperor's health, openly baiting Gui's words so he would know that Cai Jing, prefect of Kaifeng, had swordsmen lying in wait outside and that if Gui showed the slightest dissent he would be seized and executed.
translations.idiomatic: He guided Que to arrange for Gui to enter and inquire after the emperor's health, openly baiting Gui's words so he would know that Cai Jing, prefect of Kaifeng, had swordsmen lying in wait outside and that if Gui showed the slightest dissent he would be seized and executed.

sentences.zh: 既而珪言上自有子，定議立延安。

translations.literal: Thereupon Gui said the emperor had his own son, and the decision was fixed to establish Yan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Gui said the emperor had his own son, and the decision was fixed to establish Yan'an as heir.

sentences.zh: 恕益無所施，猶自謂有定策功，傳播其語。

translations.literal: Shu had even less room to act, yet still claimed credit for settling the succession and spread his words.
translations.idiomatic: Shu had even less room to act, yet still claimed credit for settling the succession and spread the story.

sentences.zh: 哲宗立，遷右司員外郎、起居舍人。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, Shu was transferred to outer-section director of the Right Secretariat and diarist.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhezong ascended the throne, Shu was transferred to outer-section director of the Right Secretariat and diarist.

sentences.zh: 又為公繪具奏，乞尊崇朱太妃，為高氏異日計。

translations.literal: He also prepared a memorial for Gong Hui requesting that Consort Zhu be honored, planning for the Gao clan's future.
translations.idiomatic: He also prepared a memorial for Gong Hui requesting that Consort Zhu be honored, planning for the Gao clan's future.

sentences.zh: 後詰之曰：「汝素不識字，誰為之者？」

translations.literal: Later the emperor questioned him: "You have never been able to read—who wrote this?"
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor questioned him: "You have never been able to read—who wrote this?"

sentences.zh: 公繪不得隱，以恕對，且上其稿。

translations.literal: Gong Hui could not conceal it, named Shu, and submitted the draft.
translations.idiomatic: Gong Hui could not conceal it, named Shu, and submitted the draft.

sentences.zh: 時恕方召試中書，遂黜知隨州，改汝、襄、河陽。

translations.literal: At the time Shu was being summoned for an examination at the Secretariat; he was then demoted to prefect of Sui Prefecture, and later transferred to Ru, Xiang, and Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Shu was being summoned for an examination at the Secretariat. He was then demoted to prefect of Sui Prefecture, and later transferred to Ru, Xiang, and Heyang.

sentences.zh: 恕久斥外，蓄怒憤，間道謁確于鄧，緒成前惡，紿司馬光子康手書，持以取信。

translations.literal: Long banished outside, Shu nursed anger and resentment, took a bypath to visit Que in Deng, picked up their old enmity, and deceived Sima Guang's son Kang into giving a letter in his own hand, which he carried to win trust.
translations.idiomatic: Long banished outside, Shu nursed anger and resentment. He took a bypath to visit Que in Deng, picked up their old enmity, and deceived Sima Guang's son Kang into giving a letter in his own hand, which he carried to win trust.

sentences.zh: 會確得罪，恕亦責監永州酒。

translations.literal: When Que fell into disgrace, Shu was also punished as supervisor of wine production in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Que fell into disgrace, Shu was also punished as supervisor of wine production in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 紹聖初，擢寶文閣待制、知青州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaosheng, he was promoted to Hanlin attendant and made prefect of Qing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shaosheng, he was promoted to Hanlin attendant and made prefect of Qing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 章惇、蔡卞得政，將甘心元祐諸人，引恕自助，召為刑部侍郎，再遷吏部尚書兼侍讀，改御史中丞。

translations.literal: When Zhang Dun and Cai Bian took power, intending to vent their spite on the Yuanyou men, they brought in Shu to assist, summoned him as vice minister of justice, then again promoted him to Minister of Personnel with concurrent duty as imperial reader, and changed his post to supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Dun and Cai Bian took power, intending to vent their spite on the Yuanyou men, they brought in Shu to assist. He was summoned as vice minister of justice, then promoted to Minister of Personnel with concurrent duty as imperial reader, and changed to supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 恕既處風憲，遂誣宣仁後有廢立謀，引司馬光言北齊婁後宣訓事，訁術高遵裕之子士京追訟其父在日，王珪令其兄士充來謀立雍王，遵裕非之。

translations.literal: Once Shu held censorial authority, he falsely accused Empress Dowager Xuanren of plotting to depose and establish an heir, citing Sima Guang's words on Empress Lou's Xuanxun in Northern Qi; he also had Gao Zunyü's son Shijing sue over his father's lifetime, saying Wang Gui had Shijing's elder brother Shichong come to plot establishing Prince Yong, which Zunyü had opposed.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shu held censorial authority, he falsely accused Empress Dowager Xuanren of plotting to depose and establish an heir, citing Sima Guang's words on Empress Lou's Xuanxun in Northern Qi. He also had Gao Zunyü's son Shijing sue over his father's lifetime, saying Wang Gui had Shijing's elder brother Shichong come to plot establishing Prince Yong, which Zunyü had opposed.

sentences.zh: 又教蔡懋上文及甫私牘為廋詞，曆詆梁燾、劉摯，雲陰圖不軌，且加司馬光、呂公著以凶悖名。

translations.literal: He also had Cai Mao submit Wen Jifu's private letters as cryptic evidence, slandering Liang Tao and Liu Zhi one by one, saying they secretly plotted rebellion, and further attached the names of treachery and defiance to Sima Guang and Lü Gongzhu.
translations.idiomatic: He also had Cai Mao submit Wen Jifu's private letters as cryptic evidence, slandering Liang Tao and Liu Zhi one by one, saying they secretly plotted rebellion, and further attached the names of treachery and defiance to Sima Guang and Lü Gongzhu.

sentences.zh: 惇使蔡京置獄于同文館，組織萬端，將悉陷諸人於族罪，既而無所得，乃已。

translations.literal: Dun had Cai Jing set up a prosecution at the Tongwen Pavilion, fabricating countless charges, intending to implicate all the men in clan-extinction crimes; when nothing was found, it was dropped.
translations.idiomatic: Dun had Cai Jing set up a prosecution at the Tongwen Pavilion, fabricating countless charges, intending to implicate all the men in clan-extinction crimes. When nothing was found, it was dropped.

sentences.zh: 恕內懷猜猾，而外持正論。

translations.literal: Inwardly Shu harbored suspicion and cunning, yet outwardly he held to upright discourse.
translations.idiomatic: Inwardly Shu harbored suspicion and cunning, yet outwardly he held to upright discourse.

sentences.zh: 嘗於經筵讀寶訓，至仁宗諭輔臣，以為人君當修舉政事，則日月薄食、星文變見為不足慮。

translations.literal: Once at the classics lecture he read the Precious Instructions; when he reached Emperor Renzong's instruction to chief ministers that a ruler should cultivate and carry out government affairs, then eclipses of sun and moon and changes in the stars were not worth worrying about.
translations.idiomatic: Once at the classics lecture he read the Precious Instructions. When he reached Emperor Renzong's instruction to chief ministers that a ruler should cultivate and carry out government affairs, then eclipses of sun and moon and changes in the stars were not worth worrying about.

sentences.zh: 恕言仁宗之旨雖合于荀卿書，然自古帝王孰肯自謂不修政事者，如此則天變遂廢矣。

translations.literal: Shu said that although Emperor Renzong's intent accorded with Xunzi's writings, since ancient times which emperor would admit he did not cultivate government affairs? If so, heavenly warnings would be abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Shu said that although Emperor Renzong's intent accorded with Xunzi's writings, since ancient times which emperor would admit he did not cultivate government affairs? If so, heavenly warnings would be abandoned.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之，數登對。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted this and repeatedly had him attend audience.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised and accepted this and repeatedly had him attend audience.

sentences.zh: 惇恐其大用，切忌之。

translations.literal: Dun feared he would be greatly employed and deeply resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Dun feared he would be greatly employed and deeply resented him.

sentences.zh: 恕亦揣帝稍薄惇，屢白其短，竟為惇所陷，出知汝州。

translations.literal: Shu also guessed the emperor had grown somewhat cool toward Dun and repeatedly reported Dun's faults; in the end he was trapped by Dun and sent out as prefect of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Shu also guessed the emperor had grown somewhat cool toward Dun and repeatedly reported Dun's faults. In the end he was trapped by Dun and sent out as prefect of Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 未幾，徙應天府。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Yingtian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to Yingtian Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 惇復摭其曩過，移知南安軍。

translations.literal: Dun again gathered his past faults and transferred him to military prefect of Nan'an.
translations.idiomatic: Dun again gathered his past faults and transferred him to military prefect of Nan'an.

sentences.zh: 徽宗初，言者論其矯誣，責為少府少監、分司西京，居均州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Huizong's reign, critics spoke of his fabrications and false accusations; he was punished as assistant director of the Palace Revenues with nominal duty in the Western Capital and lived in Jun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Emperor Huizong's reign, critics spoke of his fabrications and false accusations. He was punished as assistant director of the Palace Revenues with nominal duty in the Western Capital and lived in Jun Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蔡京當國，經營湟、鄯，以開邊隙，欲使恕立方面之勳，起為鄜延經略安撫使，旋改涇原，擢至龍圖閣學士。

translations.literal: When Cai Jing held the state, he worked on Huang and Shan to open frontier conflict and wished Shu to win frontier merit; Shu was recalled as frontier commissioner and pacification commissioner of Fuyan, soon changed to Jingyuan, and promoted to Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: When Cai Jing held the state, he worked on Huang and Shan to open frontier conflict and wished Shu to win frontier merit. Shu was recalled as frontier commissioner and pacification commissioner of Fuyan, soon changed to Jingyuan, and promoted to Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 恕乞築蕭關，采其裏人許彥圭車戰法，為淺攻計。

translations.literal: Shu requested building Xiao Pass, adopted his fellow townsman Xu Yangui's chariot-warfare method, and planned shallow attacks.
translations.idiomatic: Shu requested building Xiao Pass, adopted his fellow townsman Xu Yangui's chariot-warfare method, and planned shallow attacks.

sentences.zh: 又欲使熙河造船，直抵興、靈，以空夏國巢穴，其謀皆迂誕。

translations.literal: He also wished to have Xihe build ships to reach directly Xing and Ling, to empty the Xia state's nest; all his schemes were far-fetched and absurd.
translations.idiomatic: He also wished to have Xihe build ships to reach directly Xing and Ling, to empty the Xia state's nest. All his schemes were far-fetched and absurd.

sentences.zh: 轉運使李復言恕所為類兒戲，不可用，帝亦燭其妄，京力主之。

translations.literal: Transport commissioner Li Fu said Shu's actions were like child's play and could not be used; the emperor also saw through his folly, but Jing strongly supported him.
translations.idiomatic: Transport commissioner Li Fu said Shu's actions were like child's play and could not be used. The emperor also saw through his folly, but Jing strongly supported him.

sentences.zh: 已而夏人寇鎮戎，欲趨渭州，警奏至京師日五六，京懼，始徙恕太原，連徙永興、潁昌、真定，尋奪職。

translations.literal: Before long the Xia people raided Zhenrong and wished to press toward Wei Prefecture; alarm reports reached the capital five or six times a day. Jing grew afraid and first transferred Shu to Taiyuan, then in succession to Yongxing, Yingchang, and Zhending; soon his post was stripped.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Xia people raided Zhenrong and wished to press toward Wei Prefecture; alarm reports reached the capital five or six times a day. Jing grew afraid and first transferred Shu to Taiyuan, then in succession to Yongxing, Yingchang, and Zhending. Soon his post was stripped.

sentences.zh: 久之，復顯謨閣待制。

translations.literal: After a long time he was again made Hanlin attendant of the Xianmo Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was again made Hanlin attendant of the Xianmo Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 居實有異材，八歲為《明妃引》，黃庭堅、晁補之、張耒、秦觀、陳師道皆見而愛之。

translations.literal: His son Jushi had unusual talent; at eight he wrote "Song of Bright Consort," and Huang Tingjian, Chao Buzhi, Zhang Lei, Qin Guan, and Chen Shidao all saw it and loved it.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jushi had unusual talent. At eight he wrote "Song of Bright Consort," and Huang Tingjian, Chao Buzhi, Zhang Lei, Qin Guan, and Chen Shidao all saw it and loved it.

sentences.zh: 從恕守隨，作《南征賦》，蘇軾讀之，歎曰：「此足以藉手見古人矣。」

translations.literal: Following Shu as prefect of Sui, he wrote "Rhapsody on the Southern Campaign"; Su Shi read it and sighed: "This is enough to measure oneself against the ancients."
translations.idiomatic: Following Shu as prefect of Sui, he wrote "Rhapsody on the Southern Campaign." Su Shi read it and sighed: "This is enough to measure oneself against the ancients."

sentences.zh: 卒時年十九，有遺文曰《呻吟集》。

translations.literal: He died at nineteen; his posthumous writings were called Groaning Collection.
translations.idiomatic: He died at nineteen. His posthumous writings were called Groaning Collection.

sentences.zh: 倞及恕在時為司農丞，靖康初至少卿，奉詔館金國使。

translations.literal: Liang, while Shu was alive, was assistant director of the Ministry of Revenue; at the beginning of Jingkang he rose to vice minister and by edict was to host the Jin envoys.
translations.idiomatic: Liang, while Shu was alive, was assistant director of the Ministry of Revenue. At the beginning of Jingkang he rose to vice minister and by edict was to host the Jin envoys.

sentences.zh: 是時，肅王使斡離不軍，為所質，朝廷議亦留其使以相當，於是逾月不遣。

translations.literal: At the time Prince Su was sent to Wanyan Zonghan's army and was held hostage; the court discussed also detaining their envoys as equivalent, and for more than a month did not send them back.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Prince Su was sent to Wanyan Zonghan's army and was held hostage. The court discussed also detaining their envoys as equivalent, and for more than a month did not send them back.

sentences.zh: 都管趙倫，燕人也，性猾獪，懼不得歸，乃詐以情告倞曰：「金國有餘睹金吾者，尚領契丹精銳甚眾，貳于金人，願歸大國，可結之以圖二酋。」

translations.literal: Chief steward Zhao Lun, a man of Yan, was cunning by nature and feared he could not return; he falsely told Liang in confidence: "In the Jin state there is Yelü Dujin, who still commands many elite Khitan troops, is disloyal to the Jin, and wishes to return to our great state—we can win him over to plot against the two chieftains."
translations.idiomatic: Chief steward Zhao Lun, a man of Yan, was cunning by nature and feared he could not return. He falsely told Liang in confidence: "In the Jin state there is Yelü Dujin, who still commands many elite Khitan troops, is disloyal to the Jin, and wishes to return to our great state—we can win him over to plot against the two chieftains."

sentences.zh: 倞以聞，大臣信之，即為賜餘睹詔書授倫，納衣領中，厚與倫金帛。

translations.literal: Liang reported this; the great ministers believed it and immediately had an edict conferring favor on Dujin given to Lun, tucked into his collar, and richly rewarded Lun with gold and silk.
translations.idiomatic: Liang reported this. The great ministers believed it and immediately had an edict conferring favor on Dujin given to Lun, tucked into his collar, and richly rewarded Lun with gold and silk.

sentences.zh: 倫獻其書粘罕，粘罕大怒，以聞金主，報令深入攻討，遂復提兵南下。

translations.literal: Lun presented the letter to Wanyan Zonghan; Zonghan was greatly enraged, reported it to the Jin ruler, and the reply ordered a deep advance and attack; he then again led troops south.
translations.idiomatic: Lun presented the letter to Wanyan Zonghan. Zonghan was greatly enraged, reported it to the Jin ruler, and the reply ordered a deep advance and attack. He then again led troops south.

sentences.zh: 倞時出知岳州，詔責其始禍，削籍停官，既而京闕失守雲。

translations.literal: Liang was then sent out as prefect of Yue Prefecture; an edict blamed him for starting the disaster, struck him from the rolls and suspended his office; soon the capital fell.
translations.idiomatic: Liang was then sent out as prefect of Yue Prefecture. An edict blamed him for starting the disaster, struck him from the rolls and suspended his office. Soon the capital fell.

sentences.zh: 呂惠卿

translations.literal: Lü Huiqing
translations.idiomatic: Lü Huiqing

sentences.zh: 呂惠卿字吉甫，泉州晉江人。

translations.literal: Lü Huiqing, courtesy name Jifu, was a native of Jinjiang in Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Huiqing, courtesy name Jifu, was a native of Jinjiang in Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 父璹習吏事，為漳浦令。

translations.literal: His father Sui was skilled in administrative affairs and served as magistrate of Zhangpu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sui was skilled in administrative affairs and served as magistrate of Zhangpu.

sentences.zh: 縣處山林蔽翳間，民病瘴霧蛇虎之害，璹教民焚燎而耕，害為衰止。

translations.literal: The county lay among dense mountain forests; the people suffered from miasma, snakes, and tigers. Sui taught the people to burn and clear land for farming, and the harm declined and stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The county lay among dense mountain forests, and the people suffered from miasma, snakes, and tigers. Sui taught the people to burn and clear land for farming, and the harm declined and stopped.

sentences.zh: 通判宜州，儂智高入寇，轉運使檄璹與兵會，或勸勿行，不聽。

translations.literal: As assistant prefect of Yi Prefecture, when Nong Zhigao invaded, the transport commissioner ordered Sui to join forces; some advised him not to go, but he would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: As assistant prefect of Yi Prefecture, when Nong Zhigao invaded, the transport commissioner ordered Sui to join forces. Some advised him not to go, but he would not listen.

sentences.zh: 將二千人躡賊後以往，得首虜為多。

translations.literal: Leading two thousand men he followed in the enemy's rear and took many heads and captives.
translations.idiomatic: Leading two thousand men he followed in the enemy's rear and took many heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 為開封府司錄，鞫中人史志聰役衛卒伐木事，吏多為之地，璹窮治之，志聰以謫去。

translations.literal: As judicial recorder of Kaifeng Prefecture, he tried the matter of the inner attendant Shi Zhicong using guard soldiers to cut timber; many clerks made excuses for him, but Sui pursued the case to the end and Zhicong was demoted and removed.
translations.idiomatic: As judicial recorder of Kaifeng Prefecture, he tried the matter of the inner attendant Shi Zhicong using guard soldiers to cut timber. Many clerks made excuses for him, but Sui pursued the case to the end and Zhicong was demoted and removed.

sentences.zh: 終光祿卿。

translations.literal: He ended as Grandee of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as Grandee of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 惠卿起進士，為真州推官。

translations.literal: Huiqing rose through the jinshi examination and became investigating officer of Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Huiqing passed the jinshi examination and became investigating officer of Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 秩滿入都，見王安石，論經義，意多合，遂定交。

translations.literal: When his term ended he entered the capital, met Wang Anshi, discussed classical meaning, found their views largely agreed, and formed a friendship.
translations.idiomatic: When his term ended he entered the capital, met Wang Anshi, discussed classical meaning, found their views largely agreed, and formed a friendship.

sentences.zh: 熙甯初，安石為政，惠卿方編校集賢書籍，安石言於帝曰：「惠卿之賢，豈特今人，雖前世儒者未易比也。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xining, when Anshi took power, Huiqing was collating Jixian Academy books. Anshi said to the emperor: "Huiqing's worth—is he merely among men of today? Even Confucian scholars of former ages would not easily compare with him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xining, when Anshi took power, Huiqing was collating Jixian Academy books. Anshi said to the emperor: "Huiqing's worth—is he merely among men of today? Even Confucian scholars of former ages would not easily compare with him.

sentences.zh: 學先王之道而能用者，獨惠卿而已。」

translations.literal: Of those who study the way of the ancient kings and can apply it, Huiqing alone suffices."
translations.idiomatic: Of those who study the way of the ancient kings and can apply it, Huiqing alone suffices."

sentences.zh: 及設制置三司條例司，以為檢詳文字，事無大小必謀之，凡所建請章奏皆其筆。

translations.literal: When the Fiscal Reform Commission was established, he was made reviewer of documents; matters great and small were always planned with him, and all memorials proposing policies were in his hand.
translations.idiomatic: When the Fiscal Reform Commission was established, he was made reviewer of documents. Matters great and small were always planned with him, and all memorials proposing policies were in his hand.

sentences.zh: 擢太子中允、崇政殿說書、集賢校理，判司農寺。

translations.literal: He was promoted to palace attendant, lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, Jixian collator, and concurrent administrator of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to palace attendant, lecturer at the Chongzheng Hall, Jixian collator, and concurrent administrator of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 司馬光諫帝曰：「惠卿憸巧非佳士，使安石負謗於中外者皆其所為。

translations.literal: Sima Guang remonstrated with the emperor: "Huiqing is crafty and cunning—not a good man. All that makes Anshi bear blame at home and abroad is his doing.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Guang remonstrated with the emperor: "Huiqing is crafty and cunning—not a good man. All that makes Anshi bear blame at home and abroad is his doing.

sentences.zh: 安石賢而愎，不閑世務，惠卿為之謀主，而安石力行之，故天下並指為奸邪。

translations.literal: Anshi is worthy but obstinate and unskilled in worldly affairs; Huiqing is his chief plotter, and Anshi forcefully carries things out—therefore the realm together points to them as treacherous and wicked.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi is worthy but obstinate and unskilled in worldly affairs. Huiqing is his chief plotter, and Anshi forcefully carries things out—therefore the realm together points to them as treacherous and wicked.

sentences.zh: 近者進擢不次，大不厭眾心。」

translations.literal: Recently his promotions out of turn greatly fail to satisfy public sentiment."
translations.idiomatic: Recently his promotions out of turn greatly fail to satisfy public sentiment."

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「惠卿進對明辨，亦似美才。」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When Huiqing attends audience he is clear and discerning—he also seems a fine talent."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "When Huiqing attends audience he is clear and discerning—he also seems a fine talent."

sentences.zh: 光曰：「惠卿誠文學辨慧，然用心不正，願陛下徐察之。

translations.literal: Guang said: "Huiqing is indeed learned and clever in debate, but his intent is not upright. I wish Your Majesty would observe him slowly.
translations.idiomatic: Guang said: "Huiqing is indeed learned and clever in debate, but his intent is not upright. I wish Your Majesty would observe him slowly.

sentences.zh: 江充、李訓若無才，何以能動人主？」

translations.literal: If Jiang Chong and Li Xun had no talent, how could they have moved their rulers?"
translations.idiomatic: If Jiang Chong and Li Xun had no talent, how could they have moved their rulers?"

sentences.zh: 帝默然。

translations.literal: The emperor was silent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was silent.

sentences.zh: 光又貽書安石曰：「諂諛之士，於公今日誠有順適之快，一旦失勢，將必賣公自售矣。」

translations.literal: Guang also sent Anshi a letter saying: "Flattering men may today give you the pleasure of compliance, but once you lose power they will surely sell you to save themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Guang also sent Anshi a letter saying: "Flattering men may today give you the pleasure of compliance, but once you lose power they will surely sell you to save themselves."

sentences.zh: 安石不悅。

translations.literal: Anshi was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi was displeased.

sentences.zh: 會惠卿以父喪去，服除，召為天章閣侍講，同修起居注，進知制誥，判國子監，與王雱同修《三經新義》。

translations.literal: When Huiqing left on his father's mourning, after the mourning period he was summoned as lecturer at the Tianzhang Pavilion, co-compiler of the imperial diary, promoted to drafter of edicts, administrator of the Directorate of Education, and co-compiler with Wang Bian of New Meanings of the Three Classics.
translations.idiomatic: When Huiqing left on his father's mourning, after the mourning period he was summoned as lecturer at the Tianzhang Pavilion, co-compiler of the imperial diary, promoted to drafter of edicts, administrator of the Directorate of Education, and co-compiler with Wang Bian of New Meanings of the Three Classics.

sentences.zh: 又知諫院，為翰林學士。

translations.literal: He also directed the Remonstrance Bureau and became Hanlin academician.
translations.idiomatic: He also directed the Remonstrance Bureau and became Hanlin academician.

sentences.zh: 安石求去，惠卿使其黨變姓名，日投匭上書留之。

translations.literal: When Anshi requested to leave office, Huiqing had his faction change names and daily drop memorials in the suggestion box asking that he be kept.
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi requested to leave office, Huiqing had his faction change names and daily drop memorials in the suggestion box asking that he be kept.

sentences.zh: 安石力薦惠卿為參知政事，惠卿懼安石去，新法必搖，作書遍遺監司、郡守，使陳利害。

translations.literal: Anshi strongly recommended Huiqing as vice grand councilor. Huiqing feared that if Anshi left, the new laws would be shaken; he wrote letters and sent them everywhere to circuit commissioners and prefects, having them state benefits and harms.
translations.idiomatic: Anshi strongly recommended Huiqing as vice grand councilor. Huiqing feared that if Anshi left, the new laws would be shaken. He wrote letters and sent them everywhere to circuit commissioners and prefects, having them state benefits and harms.

sentences.zh: 又從容白帝下詔，言終不以吏違法之故，為之廢法。

translations.literal: He also calmly told the emperor to issue an edict saying that the laws would never be abolished because officials violated them.
translations.idiomatic: He also calmly told the emperor to issue an edict saying that the laws would never be abolished because officials violated them.

sentences.zh: 故安石之政，守之益堅。

translations.literal: Therefore Anshi's policies were upheld all the more firmly.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Anshi's policies were upheld all the more firmly.

sentences.zh: 議罷制科，馮京爭之不得。

translations.literal: When abolishing the decree examination was discussed, Feng Jing argued against it but could not prevail.
translations.idiomatic: When abolishing the decree examination was discussed, Feng Jing argued against it but could not prevail.

sentences.zh: 弟升卿無學術，引為侍講。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shengqing had no learning, yet Huiqing brought him in as lecturer.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shengqing had no learning, yet Huiqing brought him in as lecturer.

sentences.zh: 又用弟和卿計，制五等丁產簿，使民自供首實，尺椽寸土，檢括無遺，至雞豚亦遍抄之。

translations.literal: He also used his younger brother Heqing's plan to create five-grade household property registers, making the people report their holdings themselves; every beam and inch of land was searched out without omission, even chickens and pigs were copied everywhere.
translations.idiomatic: He also used his younger brother Heqing's plan to create five-grade household property registers, making the people report their holdings themselves. Every beam and inch of land was searched out without omission; even chickens and pigs were copied everywhere.

sentences.zh: 隱匿者許告，而以貲三之一充賞，民不勝其困。

translations.literal: Concealers were permitted to be reported, and one-third of their property was given as reward; the people could not bear the hardship.
translations.idiomatic: Concealers were permitted to be reported, and one-third of their property was given as reward. The people could not bear the hardship.

sentences.zh: 又因保甲正長給散青苗，使結甲赴官，不遺一人，上下騷動。

translations.literal: He also had baojia heads distribute green-sprout loans, making each group go together to the office without leaving out a single person; above and below were in uproar.
translations.idiomatic: He also had baojia heads distribute green-sprout loans, making each group go together to the office without leaving out a single person. Above and below were in uproar.

sentences.zh: 鄭俠疏惠卿朋奸壅蔽，惠卿怒，又惡馮京異己，而安石弟安國惡惠卿奸諂，面辱之。

translations.literal: Zheng Xia memorialized that Huiqing formed a clique of traitors and blocked the court; Huiqing was angry, also hated Feng Jing for differing from him, and Anshi's younger brother Anguo hated Huiqing's treachery and flattery and insulted him to his face.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xia memorialized that Huiqing formed a clique of traitors and blocked the court. Huiqing was angry, also hated Feng Jing for differing from him, and Anshi's younger brother Anguo hated Huiqing's treachery and flattery and insulted him to his face.

sentences.zh: 於是乘勢並陷三人，皆獲罪。

translations.literal: Thereupon he seized the opportunity to trap all three together, and all were punished.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he seized the opportunity to trap all three together, and all were punished.

sentences.zh: 安石以安國之故，始有隙。

translations.literal: Because of Anguo, Anshi first had a rift with him.
translations.idiomatic: Because of Anguo, Anshi first had a rift with him.

sentences.zh: 惠卿既叛安石，凡可以害王氏者無不為。

translations.literal: Once Huiqing turned against Anshi, there was nothing he would not do that could harm the Wang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Once Huiqing turned against Anshi, there was nothing he would not do that could harm the Wang clan.

sentences.zh: 韓絳為相不能制，請復用安石。

translations.literal: Han Jiang as chief councilor could not control him and requested that Anshi be reused.
translations.idiomatic: Han Jiang as chief councilor could not control him and requested that Anshi be reused.

sentences.zh: 安石至，猶與共事。

translations.literal: When Anshi arrived, they still worked together in office.
translations.idiomatic: When Anshi arrived, they still worked together in office.

sentences.zh: 御史蔡承禧論其惡，鄧綰又言其兄弟強借秀州富民錢買田，出知陳州。

translations.literal: Investigating censor Cai Chenxi spoke of his wickedness; Deng Wan also said his brothers forcibly borrowed money from a wealthy man in Xiu Prefecture to buy land, and Huiqing was sent out as prefect of Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Investigating censor Cai Chenxi spoke of his wickedness. Deng Wan also said his brothers forcibly borrowed money from a wealthy man in Xiu Prefecture to buy land, and Huiqing was sent out as prefect of Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 久之，以資政殿學士知延州。

translations.literal: After a long time he was made academician of the Zizheng Hall and prefect of Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time he was made academician of the Zizheng Hall and prefect of Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 始，陝西緣邊漢蕃兵各自為軍，每戰則以蕃部為先鋒，而漢兵城守，伺便乃出戰。

translations.literal: At first on the Shaanxi frontier Han and tribal troops each formed separate armies; in each battle the tribal units served as vanguard while Han troops guarded cities and went out to fight when opportunity arose.
translations.idiomatic: At first on the Shaanxi frontier Han and tribal troops each formed separate armies. In each battle the tribal units served as vanguard while Han troops guarded cities and went out to fight when opportunity arose.

sentences.zh: 惠卿始合之為一，先搜補守兵而出其選以戰，隨屯置將，具條約上之，邊人及議者多言不可。

translations.literal: Huiqing first merged them into one, first searched out and supplemented garrison troops and selected the best for battle, placed generals at each encampment, submitted detailed regulations, and frontier people and critics mostly said it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Huiqing first merged them into one, searched out and supplemented garrison troops and selected the best for battle, placed generals at each encampment, submitted detailed regulations, and frontier people and critics mostly said it could not be done.

sentences.zh: 路都監高永亨，老將也，爭之力，奏斥之。

translations.literal: Circuit commander Gao Yongheng, an old general, argued against it forcefully and memorialized to have Huiqing dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Circuit commander Gao Yongheng, an old general, argued against it forcefully and memorialized to have Huiqing dismissed.

sentences.zh: 蕃部屈全乜將入寇，惠卿以近世帥臣多養威持重，乃將牙兵按邊，啟師於東郊，遂趨綏德，抵無定河，曆十有八日而還。

translations.literal: When the tribal leader Qu Quanmie was about to invade, Huiqing thought recent frontier commanders mostly preserved prestige and held back; he therefore led his personal guard to inspect the border, opened the campaign at the eastern suburb, then pressed toward Suide, reached the Wuding River, and returned after eighteen days.
translations.idiomatic: When the tribal leader Qu Quanmie was about to invade, Huiqing thought recent frontier commanders mostly preserved prestige and held back. He therefore led his personal guard to inspect the border, opened the campaign at the eastern suburb, then pressed toward Suide, reached the Wuding River, and returned after eighteen days.

sentences.zh: 俄丁母憂，詔於本奉外特給五萬，惠卿更請添支萬五千，御史劾之，將下揚州取奉曆，帝曰：「惠卿固貪冒，然嘗為執政，治之傷體，姑責以義可也。」

translations.literal: Soon he entered mourning for his mother; an edict gave fifty thousand beyond his regular salary, and Huiqing further requested an additional fifteen thousand. Censors impeached him and were about to send officials to Yang Prefecture to fetch his salary records. The emperor said: "Huiqing is indeed greedy, but he was once in power; prosecuting him would harm dignity—for now rebuking him on principle will do."
translations.idiomatic: Soon he entered mourning for his mother. An edict gave fifty thousand beyond his regular salary, and Huiqing further requested an additional fifteen thousand. Censors impeached him and were about to send officials to Yang Prefecture to fetch his salary records. The emperor said: "Huiqing is indeed greedy, but he was once in power; prosecuting him would harm dignity—for now rebuking him on principle will do."

sentences.zh: 但削其誤奉，惠卿猶自辨，御史又論其方居喪，不應有言，詔勿問。

translations.literal: Only his improper salary was cut; Huiqing still defended himself. Censors again argued that while in mourning he should not speak; an edict ordered no further inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Only his improper salary was cut; Huiqing still defended himself. Censors again argued that while in mourning he should not speak, and an edict ordered no further inquiry.

sentences.zh: 元豐五年，加大學士、知太原府。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng he was given the title of grand academician and made prefect of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yuanfeng he was given the title of grand academician and made prefect of Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 入見，將使仍鎮鄜延。

translations.literal: On entering audience, he was about to be sent again to command Fuyan.
translations.idiomatic: On entering audience, he was about to be sent again to command Fuyan.

sentences.zh: 惠卿云：「陝西之師，非唯不可以攻，亦不可以守，要在大為形勢而已。」

translations.literal: Huiqing said: "The Shaanxi armies cannot only not attack—they also cannot defend. What matters is simply to create a great posture."
